problem: Most embodied navigation work assumes static environments with at least one collision-free path, so agents fail in obstacle-cluttered scenes where they must physically move objects aside. Existing interactive navigation agents rely on a single observation modality (2D or 3D) for scene representation.
motivation: Human environments often contain disarranged objects that block paths, so navigating efficiently requires physical interaction with the scene. 2D images and 3D observations offer complementary information, and fusing them should give RL agents a more informative representation for reasoning about interactions.
key_idea: A cross dimension scene representation module lifts 2D feature maps to 3D and aligns them with 3D observations, so an RL interactive navigation agent can fuse both modalities.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract suggests that combining 2D and 3D information yields a richer representation than either alone, which helps RL agents cope with the challenges of physical interaction.
method: 2D observation encoder: extracts features from 2D observations, producing 2D feature maps.
3D observation encoder: extracts features from 3D observations.
Joint representation network: lifts the 2D feature maps to 3D and aligns them with the 3D observation to fuse information across dimensions.
RL framework: uses the fused representation as input to the policy for interactive navigation.
